title: How to choose an icon pack
intro: An icon pack is a typeface for pictures. Choose it with the same care as the text face. These rules hold for an open-source set and for a licensed library.

rules.test: Set an icon next to the body text at text size. The line of the icon and the stem of a letter have the same weight.

rules.rule: Terminals and corners follow the radius token.
rules.test: Butt caps and mitre joins go with a radius of zero. Round caps and round joins go with a soft radius.

rules.rule: The fill mode follows the technology of the era.
rules.test: Print eras cut solid forms. Screen eras with depth fill and shade the form. Current product interfaces draw an outline.

rules.rule: The metaphors are not younger than the style.
rules.test: Each picture is an object that the era knew. An icon with a later metaphor breaks the period.
All icons come from one family and one variant, drawn on one field. Do not mix families on one surface.
List each concept that the product needs before you commit. A family that has no icon for one of them is the wrong family.
An icon takes currentColor. A second tone comes from a token, not from the file.
Read the licence of the set. Give credit where the licence asks for it. A product with a brand uses its licensed library and applies the same rules to choose the family.
